(A) One off-street parking space in addition to the off-street parking space required by GMC Chapter 17.48 (Off-Street Parking and Loading) for the primary dwel
ruling: Off-street Parking and Loading, pointed at by both dimensional tables without a number beside it. OAR 660-046-0220(2)(e)(B)(iv) caps what any Oregon city may require of middle housing at one space per unit and the state layer carries that as `preempts: cap`, so this chapter can only bind at or below the figure already screened against. Worth fetching the day this corpus screens a use the middle-housing rules do not reach.

sample: Setbacks for manufactured homes in a mobile home park are subject to the standards in GMC Section 17.62.070(4).
ruling: Setbacks for manufactured homes in a mobile home park. One sentence, printed once in each dimensional table and spanned by rowspan over every setback row, which is why it counts ten times. The pod is factory-built and is neither a manufactured dwelling nor sited on a rented space in a park, so the standard is about somebody else's building and 17.62 is not fetched.

sample: Development. Any manmade change defined as the construction of buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, paving, filling, grading or site clearing, and g
ruling: An exemption inside the definition of Development: within the Willamette and Tualatin River Protection Areas the term also reaches change of use, grading and vegetation removal "unless specifically exempted per CDC 28.040". An exemption list can only narrow what counts as development, so reading it cannot add a standard to this building. What Chapter 28 states about building inside a protection area is a separate gap and a real one -- the areas are boundaries nothing here holds, which is why the river chapters are unencoded. This reference is not what would close it.

sample: Accessory uses are allowed in this zone as provided by Chapter 34 CDC. (Ord. 1745 § 1 (Exh. A), 2023)
ruling: Accessory Structures, Accessory Dwelling Units, and Accessory Uses, and the twenty-two mentions are two sentences. Every zone chapter says "Accessory uses are allowed in this zone as provided by Chapter 34 CDC" and every zone chapter lists the chapter first among its related procedures. A quadplex is a primary use here -- "c. Quadplex residential units", a row under uses permitted outright in all nine chapters -- so nothing this screen places is an accessory anything, and the chapter is not fetched.

sample: Design exception. A discretionary decision to permit modification of a design standard or an alternative to a standard within Chapter 58 CDC (Willamette Falls D
ruling: Willamette Falls Drive Commercial Design District. Its one binding mention is the second sentence of CDC 25.070(C), which sends the buildings that subsection does not reach there: "This subsection applies only to ... residential and historically residential properties in the Willamette Historic District. Other buildings are subject to the requirements in Chapter 58 CDC." This pod is four dwellings, so it is the residential half of that sentence and Chapter 58 is the branch it does not take. Not fetched for that reason and not for the usual one -- if the catalog ever holds a ground-floor-commercial design, this becomes a real gap.

sample: Except as may otherwise be established by this code, the appropriate lot or parcel size for a conditional use shall be determined by the approval authority at t
ruling: Conditional-use lot sizing: "the appropriate lot or parcel size for a conditional use shall be determined by the approval authority at the time of consideration of the application". Its eight binding mentions are the body of each chapter''s own section headed DIMENSIONAL REQUIREMENTS, CONDITIONAL USES. A quadplex is permitted outright in every one of these zones, so the conditional-use path is not the path this building takes and the section never reaches it.

sample: 2. Transportation facilities (Type II) are those which are not designated in the adopted TSP or part of an approved, active development order. Type II transport
ruling: Type II transportation facilities -- "those which are not designated in the adopted TSP or part of an approved, active development order ... allowed in all zoning districts subject to conditional use approval and the additional criteria of CDC 60.090". A road, not a dwelling. Both binding mentions are inside Chapter 2''s definition of a transportation facility.

sample: Type I and II lands shall not be counted toward lot area when determining allowable floor area ratio, except that a minimum floor area ratio of 0.30 shall be al
ruling: Non-conforming Structures, and every one of the nineteen mentions is one of two sentences. Eight are the zone chapters' own list of related procedures ("2. Chapter 66 CDC, Non-conforming Structures"); the rest are the tail of the Type I and II lands sentence, which lets an existing house over the FAR be rebuilt to its prior dimensions after damage without a non-conforming structures permit. Neither reaches a new building on a lot, which is the only thing this screen places, so the chapter is not fetched.

sample: 5. Chapter 75 CDC, Variance. (Ord. 1745 § 1 (Exh. A), 2023)
ruling: Variance. Every mention is an item in a zone chapter''s list of related procedures, beside Chapters 34, 44 and 66 -- declined relief rather than a standard. Relief is modelled in the score stage, not encoded here: a pod one foot over a setback is a lot with an application attached. Worth recording that the historic district removes even that. CDC 25.080(A): "The provisions of Chapter 75 CDC, Variance, shall not apply to the standards in this chapter", and what stands in its place is a discretionary modification turning on historical records.
